Rashi on Nedarim 55a:1:1.english: Only from the five species - Wheat, barley, spelt, rye, and oats.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:1:2.hebrew: רבי מאיר אומר בו' - בהא ודאי מודינא לך, שהנודר מן התבואה אינו אסור אלא מחמשת מינין, אבל הנודר מן הדגן אסור בכל מין; דמידגן משמע דבר שעושין ממנו כר, ופול המצרי יבש עושין ממנו כרי, ולהכי אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:1:2.english: Rabbi Meir says, etc. - In this [matter] I certainly agree with you that one who vows [not to benefit] from grain [tevua] is prohibited only from the five species [of grain], but one who vows [not to benefit] from dagan is prohibited from every species; for meidegan [being heaped, i.e., dagan] implies something from which they make a pile, and from dry cowpea they make a pile, and therefore it is prohibited.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:1.hebrew: למימרא דדגן - דכתיב בקרא, כל מין דמידגן משמע, וחייב במעשר מן התורה ואפי' משאר מינין, מדקתני: הנודר מן הדגן אסור בכל:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:1.english: Is this to say that dagan - [that] which is written in the verse means any species that is piled up, and is obligated in tithes by Torah law even from other species, since [the Mishnah] teaches: "One who vows [not to benefit] from dagan is prohibited from all [of them]"?

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:2.hebrew: וכפרוץ הדבר - כלומר, קיבלו עליהם תקנתא של חזקיהו לעשר הכל, כדכתיב "הרבו בני ישראל וגו'". אי אמרת בשלמא דדגן לא משמע אלא מחמשת מינין, היינו דאתא קרא למימר "הרבו בני ישראל", דאפי' דבר שלא נתחייב במעשר מן התורה — כגון שאר מיני דמידגני — היו מעשרים, כדי להחזיק בתקנה; אלא אי אמרת דגן כל מיני דמידגן משמע, מאי "וכפרוץ הדבר הרבו"? כלומר, מה הוסיפו על מה שכתוב בתורה:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:2.english: And as soon as the matter was publicized - That is to say, they accepted upon themselves Hezekiah's enactment to tithe everything, as it is written, "the children of Israel gave in abundance, etc." Granted, if you say that dagan refers only to the five species [of grain], that is why the verse comes to say "the children of Israel gave in abundance," [teaching] that even something that was not obligated in tithes by Torah law — such as other species that are placed in a pile — they would tithe, in order to uphold the enactment. But if you say [that] dagan means all species that are placed in a pile, what is [the meaning of] "And as soon as the matter was publicized, [they] gave in abundance"? That is to say, what did they add beyond what is written in the Torah?

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:3.hebrew: אמר אביי - כל דמידגן משמע, ומאי ״וכפרוץ הדבר הרבו״? לאיתויי פירות האילן וירק, דהרבו בו בני ישראל ליתן מהן מעשר, דמדאורייתא לא מחייב במעשר אלא מידי דמידגן, דלא משמע אלא מחמשת מינין:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:2:3.english: Abaye said - [Indeed, dagan] implies anything that is piled up; and what is [the meaning of] "And as soon as the matter was publicized, they gave in abundance"? [It comes] to include fruits of the tree and vegetables, from which the children of Israel gave in abundance to give tithes — for by Torah law, one is only obligated in tithes for something that is piled up, which implies only [produce] from the five species [of grain].

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:4:1.hebrew: ותבואת השדה לרוב - אלמא דתבואה משמע כל מילי, דהא דכתיב ותבואת השדה לאו מחמשת מינין דאיקרו תבואה: תבואה סתם לא משמע אלא מחמשת מינין, תבואת השדה משמע כל מידי הגדל מן השדה:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:4:1.english: And the produce of the field in abundance - Thus [we see] that tevua [produce] implies all things, for that which is written, "and the produce of the field," is not of the five species [of grain] that are called tevua. Unqualified tevua implies only [produce] of the five species, [whereas] "tevua of the field" implies anything that grows from the field.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:5:2.hebrew: היכי מיקריא - כלומר, ממה אגבה אותו ממון:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:5:2.english: How is it called - That is to say, from what shall I collect that money?

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:5:3.english: Only from five species - And he collects only from [the] five species.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:5:4.hebrew: עללתא - משמע כל מילי שעולה ומשבח, ואפי' משאר פירות שמשבחין צוה לגבות מהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:5:4.english: Alalta - [This] means anything that grows and yields, and even from other produce that yields, he commanded to collect from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:1.english: They returned it before Rava - [They returned] that answer.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:2.english: Rent of houses and rent of boats - Does [he] collect from them or not?

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:3.english: Do we say: Since they depreciate - [That is,] they diminish [in value] as they grow old.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:4.hebrew: לאו עללתא - מיקרו, שאין עולה ומשביח, ולא גבי מינייהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:4.english: Not alalta - [They are] called [so], because [it] does not rise and improve, and [he] does not collect from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:5.hebrew: או דילמא כיון דלא ידיע פחתייהו - שעל יד על יד מתחסר, ואינו ניכר פחיתותו להדיא; והואיל ונוטל הימנו שכר, עולה ומשביח הוי, ויהבו ליה מההוא אגרא:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:5.english: Or perhaps, since their depreciation is not apparent - For it diminishes little by little, and its depreciation is not directly noticeable; and since he takes rent from it, it is [considered] something that increases and appreciates, and they give him from that rent.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:6.hebrew: אמרוה קמיה דרב יוסף - הא דאמר רבא, דהא לא מיבעיא ליה דעללתא כל מידי משמע:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:6:6.english: They stated it before Rav Yosef - [Namely,] that which Rava said, that this was not a dilemma for him, that alalta means everything.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:7:1.english: [It] is similar to the dilution of Rava - For when Rava was studying before him, he would dilute [wine] for him in this manner.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:8:1.hebrew: לא תיתיב אכרעך כו' - לפי שהגיס לבו, שאל לו מקרא זה כדי להשפיל דעתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 55a:8:1.english: Do not sit on your feet, etc. - Because he had become haughty, [Rav Yosef] asked him [about] this verse in order to humble his spirit.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:9:1.english: Like a wilderness that is ownerless to all - [He] teaches Torah free of charge to all.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:9:2.english: Nahaliel - The Torah becomes like an inheritance for him.

Rashi on Nedarim 55a:9:3.english: That they sink it into the ground - Like a lintel.

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:1:1.hebrew: מתניתין אסור בפול המצרי - דכל מידי דאידגן, שמעמידין אותו בכרי, נקרא דגן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:1:1.english: The Mishnah: "[He] is prohibited from [eating] the Egyptian bean" - For anything that is heaped [de'idgan], meaning that they stack it in a pile, is called dagan.

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:2:1.hebrew: וכפרוץ הדבר - פסוק הוא בדברי הימים, שתיקן חזקיהו שיביאו המעשרות לאוצר לבית המקדש, וכפרוץ תקנתו הרבו בני ישראל מעשר דגן תירוש ויצהר וכל תבואת שדה לרוב. והשתא ס"ד דכל תבואת שדה, כלומר כגון פול המצרי; אסיפא דקרא סמיך, דכתיב: "כל תבואת שדה לרוב". ואי דגן כל מילי דאידגן משמע, ל"ל למיכתב "כל תבואת שדה"? ונהי דדגן דכתיב באורייתא, "מעשר דגנך", לא משמע אלא ה' מינין, מיהו ההוא דדברי הימים משמע כל מילי — דאי בלשון ב"א משמע כל מידי דמדגן, ההוא נמי משמע כל מילי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:2:1.english: "And as soon as the matter was publicized" - This is a verse in Chronicles, [describing] that Hezekiah instituted that they bring the tithes to the storehouse in the Temple, and when his enactment spread, the children of Israel gave in abundance the tithe of dagan, wine, and oil, and all the produce of the field in abundance. Now, [Rav Yosef] initially thought that "all the produce of the field" [includes things] such as Egyptian beans; he is relying on the end of the verse, as it is written, "all the produce of the field in abundance." And if dagan means anything that is piled up, why did [Scripture] need to write "all the produce of the field"? And granted that dagan which is written in the Torah — [namely,] "the tithe of your dagan" — means only the five species [of grain], nevertheless, that [mention of dagan] in Chronicles means all things [that are piled up], for if in people's speech [dagan] means anything that is piled up, that [verse] also means all things [that are piled up].

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:3:1.hebrew: הכל מודים - אפילו רבנן, שאין אסור אלא מה' מינין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:3:1.english: Everyone concedes - Even the Rabbis [concede] that he is prohibited only from the five species [of grain]:

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:4:1.hebrew: מתיב רב יוסף - וה"ה לרבי מאיר דמתני' מותיב, ואמר אביי: "לאיתויי פירות האילן וירק":
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:4:1.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection - And the same applies to Rabbi Meir of the Mishnah — he is raising an objection [against him as well]; and Abaye said [above]: "To include fruits of the tree and vegetables."

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:4:2.english: "Tevua of the field is discrete" - For [it] certainly implies all things.

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:5:1.english: Alalta - It means every kind [of produce] that is heaped up.

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:6:1.hebrew: הא לא מיבעיא ליה - דכל פירות איקרי עללתא, כל דבר אוכלין מקרי עללתא, וכן שאר נכסים, דעללתא מידי דהוא בעין משמע. כי קמיבעיא ליה: שכר בתים שכר ספינות — מי אמרינן: כיון דבתים וספינות פוחתים בכל יום ומשתנים, לאו בכלל עללתא, דעללתא משמע מידי דמשבח ולא מידי דפוחת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:6:1.english: That was not a dilemma for him - [meaning] that all produce is called alalta; every item of food is called alalta, and likewise other property, for alalta implies something that exists in substance. When he had a dilemma, [it was regarding] rent of houses [and] rent of boats — do we say: since houses and boats depreciate every day and deteriorate, [their rent] is not included in alalta, because alalta implies something that appreciates and not something that depreciates?

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:6:2.hebrew: או דלמא כיון דלא ידיע פחתייהו - פי': שפוחתין מעט מעט ולזמן מרובה, ה"ל [מידי] דמשבח, ואיקרי שפיר עללתא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:6:2.english: Or perhaps, since their depreciation is not conspicuous - Meaning: since they depreciate little by little and over a long time, it is [something] that increases in value, and is properly called alalta [a crop].

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:9:1.english: That he be open to all - that he teach Torah to everyone:

Tosafot on Nedarim 55a:9:2.english: That they lower [sheshokefin] - [This is] an expression of a trampled threshold [iskopa].
